en: avoiding greater misfortune with lesser sacrifice

examples.en: I tripped on the street, but I'll think of it as getting my bad luck out of the way.
Think of this accident as a small price paid to ward off worse luck.

examples.ko: 시험 전에 지갑을 잃어버린 게 액땜이면 좋겠어요.
examples.en: I hope losing my wallet before the exam is the small bad luck that spares me a bigger one.

examples.ko: 컵을 깬 걸 액땜으로 치기로 했어요.
examples.en: I decided to count breaking the cup as my bit of bad luck out of the way.

examples.ko: 액땜 한번 크게 했으니 이제 잘될 거예요.
examples.en: You've had your share of bad luck, so things will go well now.

examples.ko: 이사 전에 작은 사고가 난 건 액땜일 거예요.
examples.en: The small accident before the move must be a bit of bad luck to ward off worse.

explain: 작은 나쁜 일을 겪어서 큰 불행을 막았다고 위로하는 말이에요. 보통 '액땜했다고 생각해'처럼 나쁜 일이 생긴 뒤에 말해요.

phrases.en: Falling today was just getting my bad luck out of the way.
phrases.nuance_ko: '액땜'에 '하다'를 붙여 작은 불행을 겪었다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 하다 to 액땜 to say you went through a small misfortune.
phrases.en_equiv: to get bad luck out of the way

phrases.en: My phone broke, but I think of it as a lesser price for avoiding worse luck.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나쁜 일이 생긴 뒤 자신이나 남을 위로할 때 가장 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common way to console yourself or others after something bad happens.
phrases.en_equiv: to look at it as paying off bad luck

phrases.en: For something meant to be a small price, it was too big.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일이 액땜이라고 하기에는 너무 크거나 힘들었다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something was too big or hard to call a mere minor misfortune.
phrases.en_equiv: for a small price of bad luck

explain_en: It is a comforting idea that a small misfortune has spared you from a bigger one. People usually say things like '액땜했다고 생각해' after something bad happens.

examples.en: Try estimating the length by eye.

examples.ko: 사람이 몇 명쯤 올지 어림하기 어려워요.
examples.en: It's hard to guess roughly how many people will come.

examples.ko: 대충 어림해도 오천 원은 넘을 거예요.
examples.en: Even a rough estimate says it will be over five thousand won.
I judged the weight of the bag by hand and told them.
I estimated the time and set out, and I wasn't late.
The value I estimated was almost the same as the real one.

explain: 정확히 재지 않고 대충 짐작해서 헤아린다는 뜻이에요. 일상에서는 '어림잡다'나 '어림짐작'이 더 자주 들리고, '어림없다'와는 뜻이 달라요.

phrases.example: 한 시간 안에 이 많은 일을 끝내겠다고요? 어림도 없어요.
phrases.en: You think you can finish all this in an hour? No way.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가능성이 전혀 없다고 강하게 말할 때 써요. 상대의 기대나 요구를 단호하게 거절하는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say something is completely out of the question. It firmly rejects someone's hope or demand.

explain_en: It means roughly gauging something without measuring it exactly. In daily talk '어림잡다' and '어림짐작' are heard more often, and '어림없다' has a different meaning.

gh: estimate or presume from evidence, formal

p.n: 어림하다 is a rough measure by eye; 짐작하다 is a general guess.

t90.ax: Try estimating the length by eye.

examples.en: It is only human for parents to worry about their children.

examples.ko: 어려운 사람을 보면 돕고 싶은 게 인지상정이죠.
examples.en: It's natural human feeling to want to help someone in need.

examples.ko: 실수한 친구를 이해해 주는 것이 인지상정 아니겠어요?
examples.en: Isn't understanding a friend who made a mistake just human nature?

examples.ko: 좋은 물건을 보면 갖고 싶은 것도 인지상정이에요.
examples.en: Wanting to own something nice when you see it is also human nature.

examples.ko: 그 마음이 인지상정이라 누구도 탓할 수 없어요.
examples.en: That feeling is only human, so no one can blame you for it.

examples.ko: 인지상정으로 한 번쯤은 봐줘도 되지 않을까요?
examples.en: Out of simple human kindness, couldn't we let it slide just once?

explain: '~는 것은 인지상정이다' 꼴로 많이 써요. '당연하다'보다 '사람이라면 누구나 그렇게 느낀다'는 점을 강조해서 주로 감정이나 인정에 관한 일에 써요.

phrases.en: It is only human to worry when your child is sick.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해요체 서술 형태로, 누구나 그렇다는 걸 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite statement explaining that anyone would feel this way.

phrases.example: 좋은 일이 있으면 자랑하고 싶은 게 인지상정이죠.
phrases.en: Wanting to brag about good news is only human, isn't it?
phrases.nuance_ko: '-죠'로 말하면 상대도 공감할 거라고 가볍게 동의를 구하는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Ending with -죠 lightly asks the listener to agree.

phrases.example: 저는 도움을 청하는 사람을 돕는 게 인지상정이라고 생각해요.
phrases.en: I think helping someone who asks for help is only human.
phrases.nuance_ko: 내 의견으로 말할 때 쓰는 문장이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A sentence for giving your own opinion.

explain_en: It is often used in the pattern '~는 것은 인지상정이다'. Rather than simply saying something is 'natural', it stresses that any person would feel that way, so it mostly goes with emotions and human sympathy.

examples.en: They say dreams are influenced by the subconscious.

examples.ko: 잠재의식 속에 불안이 남아 있었나 봐요.
examples.en: Anxiety must have remained in my subconscious.
Those words stayed deep in my subconscious.
I heard that ads stimulate the subconscious.

examples.ko: 잠재의식은 우리도 모르게 행동에 영향을 줘요.
examples.en: The subconscious affects our actions without us knowing.
If I repeat positive words, will my subconscious change?

explain: '무의식'과 비슷하게 쓰이지만, 일상 대화에서는 '나도 모르게 마음속에 있는 생각'이라는 느낌으로 말할 때 많이 써요. 심리나 자기계발 이야기에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.example: 잠재의식 속에 오래된 기억이 남아 있어요.
phrases.en: An old memory remains in my subconscious.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마음 깊은 곳을 가리킬 때 자주 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common way to point to the depths of the mind.

phrases.example: 광고는 잠재의식에 영향을 줄 수 있어요.
phrases.en: Ads can influence the subconscious.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자기도 모르게 받는 영향을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for influences we aren't aware of.

phrases.en: The words came out without my realizing it.
phrases.nuance_ko: '잠재의식'은 마음속에 있는 생각을 말하고, '무의식중에'는 '나도 모르게'라는 뜻으로 행동이나 말에 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The headword refers to thoughts lying in the mind, while '무의식중에' means 'without realizing' and attaches to an action or a remark.

explain_en: It is close to '무의식' (the unconscious), but in everyday talk it often means thoughts lying in your mind without you realizing. It comes up a lot in psychology and self-improvement topics.

examples.ko: 이 우산은 양산 겸용이라서 여름에도 잘 써요.
examples.en: This umbrella doubles as a parasol, so I use it in summer too.

examples.ko: 남녀 겸용 신발이라서 누구나 신을 수 있어요.
examples.en: These are unisex shoes, so anyone can wear them.
This desk is a dual-use one that also works as a dining table.

examples.ko: 겸용은 편하지만 기능마다 조금씩 아쉬울 수 있어요.
examples.en: Dual-purpose items are convenient, but each function can be a little disappointing.

examples.ko: 충전기가 노트북과 휴대폰 겸용으로 나와서 짐이 줄었어요.
examples.en: The charger works for both laptop and phone, so my luggage got lighter.

examples.ko: 겸용 가방이라 백팩으로도 크로스백으로도 들 수 있어요.
examples.en: It's a convertible bag, so you can carry it as a backpack or a crossbody.

explain: '양산 겸용 우산'처럼 두 이름 사이에 넣어 한 물건이 두 가지로 쓰인다고 말해요. 반대로 한 가지 용도만 있으면 '전용'이라고 해요. 사람이나 역할에는 '겸'을 써서 '총무 겸 회계'처럼 말해요.

phrases.en: It's a dual-use product, so buying just one is enough.
phrases.nuance_ko: 두 가지 일을 한꺼번에 하는 물건을 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes an item that does two jobs at once.

phrases.example: 이 방은 침실과 서재 겸용으로 써요.
phrases.en: I use this room as both a bedroom and a study.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 공간이나 물건을 두 가지 용도로 쓸 때 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when one space or item serves two purposes.

phrases.example: 저는 동아리에서 총무 겸 회계를 맡고 있어요.
phrases.en: In my club I serve as both secretary and treasurer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 두 역할을 함께 맡을 때는 '겸용' 대신 '겸'을 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: For one person with two roles, use '겸' instead of '겸용'.

explain_en: Put it after two names, as in '양산 겸용 우산', to say one object serves two purposes. The opposite, a single purpose only, is '전용'. For people or roles, use '겸' instead, as in '총무 겸 회계'.

en: to be even; to be in a line

examples.ko: 책상 두 개를 나란하게 붙여 놓았어요.
examples.en: I put two desks side by side.
Please line up in two parallel rows.

examples.ko: 두 산줄기가 나란해서 길도 같은 방향으로 나 있어요.
examples.en: The two mountain ridges run in parallel, so the road also runs in the same direction.

examples.ko: 책상이 나란하지 않아서 줄을 다시 맞췄어요.
examples.en: The desks weren't in line, so I lined them up again.

examples.ko: 길과 강이 나란하다고 들어서 쉽게 찾았어요.
examples.en: I heard the road and the river run side by side, so I found it easily.

examples.ko: 두 선이 나란하면 끝까지 만나지 않아요.
examples.en: If two lines are parallel, they never meet.

explain: 대화에서는 '나란히 앉다', '나란히 서다'처럼 '나란히' 모양으로 자주 들려요. 앞뒤가 아니라 옆으로 가지런히 놓이거나 같은 방향으로 이어지는 모양을 말해요. 한 줄로 서는 '일렬로'와는 달라요.

phrases.example: 우리나라 기술이 이제 선진국과 어깨를 나란히 해요.
phrases.en: Our country's technology is now on a par with developed countries.
phrases.nuance_ko: 실제 어깨가 아니라 힘이나 수준이 서로 비슷하다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It does not mean actual shoulders; it means being equal in strength or level.
phrases.en_equiv: stand shoulder to shoulder with; be on a par with

explain_en: In conversation you often hear the form '나란히', as in '나란히 앉다' (sit side by side) and '나란히 서다'. It describes things placed neatly beside each other, or running in the same direction, rather than front to back. It differs from '일렬로', which means in a single line.

t90.ax: I put two desks side by side.

examples.en: This coin is made of copper and nickel.

examples.ko: 니켈 알레르기가 있어서 금속 귀걸이를 못 해요.
examples.en: I have a nickel allergy, so I can't wear metal earrings.
A lot of nickel is used in electric car batteries.

examples.ko: 니켈 가격이 오르면서 배터리 값도 올랐대요.
examples.en: I heard battery prices went up as the price of nickel rose.
Stainless steel contains chromium and nickel.

examples.ko: 새로 산 시계가 니켈 도금이라서 반짝반짝해요.
examples.en: My new watch is nickel-plated, so it's really shiny.

explain: 동전, 배터리, 도금, 스테인리스 같은 말과 함께 자주 들어요. 금속 알레르기를 일으키는 금속으로도 잘 알려져 있고, 뉴스에서는 원자재 가격 이야기에 나와요.

phrases.example: 이 열쇠고리는 니켈 도금이 되어 있어요.
phrases.en: This key ring is nickel-plated.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건 겉에 니켈을 얇게 입힌 것을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a thin layer of nickel is coated on an object.

phrases.example: 니켈 가격이 올라서 배터리 값도 올랐어요.
phrases.en: Nickel prices went up, so battery prices rose too.
phrases.nuance_ko: 원자재 뉴스에서 자주 나오는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A phrase often seen in raw-material news.

phrases.en: This coin contains nickel.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 물건 안에 니켈이 섞여 있다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say that nickel is included in something.

explain_en: You often hear it together with coins, batteries, plating and stainless steel. It is also well known as a metal that causes allergies, and in the news it appears in stories about raw material prices.

en: to be neat; to be clean

examples.en: That man has a clean-cut face.

examples.ko: 머리를 자르고 나니 훨씬 멀끔해 보여요.
examples.en: After getting a haircut, you look much neater.
The room looks so tidy after cleaning that I feel good.
I went to the interview dressed neatly.
After I shaved, my face looked clean.
The windows look really clean now that I wiped them.

explain: 사람의 얼굴이나 옷차림이 지저분하지 않고 단정할 때 많이 써요. 물건이나 방이 깨끗하게 정리된 모습에도 쓸 수 있어요. '말끔하다'와 비슷하게 쓰고, 반대말은 '지저분하다'예요.

phrases.example: 새 옷을 입으니 훨씬 멀끔해 보여요.
phrases.en: You look much neater in new clothes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉모습이 깔끔하다는 인상을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the impression of looking neat and tidy.

phrases.en: A clean-faced staff member greeted me.
phrases.nuance_ko: '멀끔한'이 뒤에 오는 명사를 꾸며서 단정한 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: '멀끔한' describes the noun after it, meaning a tidy look.

phrases.en: After cleaning, the room is spotless.
phrases.nuance_ko: '멀끔하다'의 작은말로 뜻이 거의 같고, 깨끗이 치운 방이나 단정한 모습에 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The smaller-sounding counterpart of '멀끔하다' with almost the same meaning; often used for a freshly cleaned room or a tidy look.

explain_en: It is often used when a person's face or outfit looks tidy and not messy. You can also use it for things or rooms that are cleaned up. It is used much like '말끔하다', and the opposite is '지저분하다'.

t90.ax: That man has a clean-cut face.

examples.en: After I wiped the floor, it shines glossily.
The marbles were so glossy that I wanted them.
I polished my shoes until they shone and went to the interview.
I picked an apple with a glossy shine.
The railing has been worn smooth and shiny by many hands.
The baby's cheeks are glowing and smooth.

explain: 매끈하고 윤이 나는 모양을 소리처럼 흉내 낸 말이에요. 잘 닦은 물건에도, 오래 만져서 닳은 물건에도 써요. '반들반들'과 비슷하고, '윤이 나다'와 자주 같이 나와요.

phrases.en: The new shoes are glossy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부사에 '하다'가 붙은 형용사 형태예요. 상태를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: An adjective formed by adding 하다 to the adverb; it describes a state.

phrases.en: I picked up a smooth, shiny stone at the river.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오래 닳아서 매끈해진 물건을 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe an object worn smooth over time.

phrases.en: I wiped the desk and now it shines.
phrases.nuance_ko: '반질반질'과 거의 같은 뜻으로 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Almost the same meaning as 반질반질 and can replace it.

explain_en: It imitates the look of a smooth, shiny surface. It works for well-polished things and for things worn smooth by long handling. It is close to '반들반들' and often appears with '윤이 나다'.

t90.ax: I picked an apple with a glossy shine.

examples.en: When sunlight passes through a prism, rainbow colors appear.
We did a prism experiment in science class.
A prism is a triangular shape made of glass.

examples.ko: 책상 위 프리즘이 빛을 여러 색으로 나눠요.
examples.en: The prism on the desk splits light into many colors.
The children made a rainbow with a prism.
The light shining through the prism spread over the wall.

explain: 과학 수업에서 빛을 여러 색으로 나눌 때 나오는 도구예요. '프리즘을 통과하다'처럼 써요. 일상 대화에서는 거의 안 쓰고, 관점을 비유하는 글에서 드물게 나와요.

phrases.example: 빛이 프리즘을 통과하면 여러 색으로 나뉘어요.
phrases.en: When light passes through a prism, it splits into many colors.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과학 설명에서 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common phrase in science explanations.

phrases.example: 오늘 과학 시간에 프리즘 실험을 해요.
phrases.en: We do a prism experiment in science class today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 수업이나 실험 이야기에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about class or experiments.

phrases.en: I shined light through a glass prism.
phrases.nuance_ko: 프리즘의 재료를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Names the material of the prism.

explain_en: The tool in science class that splits light into colors. You say '프리즘을 통과하다'. It is rare in everyday speech and appears only occasionally as a metaphor for a point of view in writing.

t90.ax: The children made a rainbow with a prism.

examples.en: This year the number of customers doubled compared to last year.
I was surprised that prices went up by double.

examples.ko: 이 가게는 양이 다른 곳의 갑절이에요.
examples.en: This shop gives double the amount of other places.

examples.ko: 시험 때문에 평소보다 갑절은 더 열심히 공부했어요.
examples.en: Because of the exam, I studied twice as hard as usual.

examples.ko: 이번 달 전기 요금이 갑절 가까이 나왔어요.
examples.en: This month's electricity bill came out at nearly double.
Pour in more water until it doubles.

explain: '두 배'와 같은 말이에요. 일상에서는 '두 배'를 더 많이 쓰고, '갑절'은 말이나 글에서 조금 예스럽고 정겨운 느낌이 있어요. 세 배, 네 배에는 쓰지 않고 꼭 두 배일 때만 써요.

phrases.en: The price of lunch has doubled.
phrases.nuance_ko: '갑절'과 같은 뜻이고 일상에서는 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 갑절, and more common in daily life.

phrases.example: 몇 년 사이에 집값이 갑절이 됐어요.
phrases.en: House prices doubled within a few years.
phrases.nuance_ko: 원래 값보다 두 배가 되었다는 변화를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a change to double the original amount.

phrases.example: 이 그릇에는 저 그릇보다 밥이 갑절이나 많아요.
phrases.en: This bowl has twice as much rice as that one.
phrases.nuance_ko: '이나'를 붙이면 생각보다 많다는 느낌이 들어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 이나 gives a feeling of 'more than expected'.

explain_en: It means the same as '두 배' (twice as much). In daily life '두 배' is more common, and '갑절' sounds a little old-fashioned and warm. It is only for exactly double, not for three or four times.

t90.ax: Pour in more water until it doubles.

examples.ko: 정확한 값은 몰라도 근사치는 말할 수 있어요.
examples.en: I don't know the exact value, but I can give an approximate one.

examples.ko: 계산기 없이 근사치부터 먼저 구해 봐요.
examples.en: Let's first work out an approximate value without a calculator.

examples.ko: 이건 근사치일 뿐이니까 정확한 숫자는 아니에요.
examples.en: This is only an approximation, so it isn't the exact number.

examples.ko: 제가 계산한 값은 실제 값에 가까운 근사치였어요.
examples.en: The value I calculated was a close approximation of the real value.
We usually write the approximate value of pi as 3.14.
Shall we compare the approximation with the actual value?

explain: 수학이나 통계에서 정확한 값 대신 가깝게 쓰는 수를 말해요. 일상에서는 '대략', '어림잡아'처럼 말하고, '근사치'는 숫자를 다루는 상황에서 더 자주 써요.

phrases.en: Let me calculate with an approximate value first.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정확하지 않아도 가까운 수로 계산할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when calculating with a close value instead of an exact one.

phrases.en: Try to find an approximate value of the answer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정확한 값 대신 가까운 수를 찾을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when finding a close number instead of the exact value.

phrases.en: Roughly a hundred people came.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 '근사치' 대신 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier everyday alternative to 근사치.

explain_en: It is a number used instead of the exact value, mainly in math and statistics. In daily talk people say '대략' or '어림잡아', and '근사치' fits situations dealing with numbers.

t90.ax: We usually write the approximate value of pi as 3.14.

examples.en: It takes twenty minutes at most to get there.

examples.ko: 이 가방은 기껏해야 만 원쯤 할 거예요.
examples.en: This bag would be worth ten thousand won at best.

examples.ko: 저는 기껏해야 일주일에 한 번 운동해요.
examples.en: I exercise once a week at the most.

examples.ko: 손님은 기껏해야 열 명 정도 올 거예요.
examples.en: At most about ten guests will come.
Even when angry, all I did was sigh.

examples.ko: 그 아이는 기껏해야 열 살쯤 됐을 거예요.
examples.en: That child must be ten years old at most.

explain: '겨우', '고작'과 비슷한데, 기껏해야는 '~쯤이다', '~밖에 안 되다', '~뿐이다'처럼 많지 않다는 말과 같이 와요. 가능한 최대치를 말하면서 '별것 아니다'라는 느낌을 줘요.

phrases.en: It's only five thousand won at most.
phrases.nuance_ko: '~밖에 안 되다'와 함께 쓰면 많지 않다는 느낌이 분명해져요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '~밖에 안 되다', the sense of 'not much' becomes clear.

phrases.en: There are only one or two people at most.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이나 물건의 수가 적다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say the number of people or things is small.

phrases.en: It only takes ten minutes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비슷한 말이에요. 고작은 '겨우 그것뿐'이라는 느낌으로, 적거나 작다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A similar word; 고작 carries the feeling of 'only that much' and is used to say something is small or little.

explain_en: It is close to 겨우 and 고작, but 기껏해야 goes with endings that say the amount is small, like ~쯤이다, ~밖에 안 되다, and ~뿐이다. It names the maximum possible amount while implying that it is no big deal.

t90.ax: I exercise once a week at the most.

examples.en: It is a little over an hour from home to school.

examples.ko: 그 일은 한 달 남짓한 시간이 걸렸어요.
examples.en: The work took a little over a month.
A man just over 170 centimeters tall came.
A little over ten friends gathered.
You will arrive in a little over thirty minutes.
I lived here for a little over five years.

explain: '남짓하다'는 수나 양 뒤에 붙어서 '그것보다 조금 더 많다'고 말해요. 보통 '한 시간 남짓', '열 명 남짓'처럼 숫자 바로 뒤에 써요. '정도'는 많거나 적을 수 있지만 '남짓'은 조금 넘는 쪽이에요.

phrases.en: I waited for my friend for a little over an hour.
phrases.nuance_ko: 숫자 바로 뒤에 붙여서 '그 숫자보다 조금 넘는다'고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Attached right after a number to say it is slightly more than that amount.

phrases.example: 교실에 학생이 열 명 남짓 있어요.
phrases.en: There are a little over ten students in the classroom.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람 수 뒤에 붙여서 '열 명보다 조금 많다'는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used after a number of people to mean slightly more than that number.

phrases.example: 집 앞에 백 미터 남짓한 길이 있어요.
phrases.en: In front of my house there is a road a little over a hundred meters long.
phrases.nuance_ko: '남짓한'으로 활용해서 뒤에 오는 명사를 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The form '남짓한' modifies the noun that follows it.
phrases.en_equiv: a road a little over 100 meters

explain_en: 남짓하다 comes right after a number or amount and means a bit more than it, as in 한 시간 남짓 or 열 명 남짓. 정도 can be a bit more or a bit less, but 남짓 only leans slightly over.
